task_instruction:
# Task: review the AI agent's summary of Lark & Lantern Bakery Ltd

*This is a practice round. It is not scored. Use it to get used to the screen and ask any questions.*

## Your role

You are a credit analyst at Aldermoor Commercial Bank. Lark & Lantern Bakery Ltd is a business client of the bank. The client has asked for a loan.

You delegated the reading to an AI agent. You asked it to:

1. summarise the client's documents,
2. pick out the important information, and
3. flag anything that differs from last year's record.

The agent has produced a draft summary. **The draft cannot be used until you have reviewed it and made a decision on it.**

## The client documents

- **D1**: Client Information and Loan Request Form
- **D2**: Previous-Year Review Note

## What to do

1. Read the agent's summary.
2. Check what it says against the client documents.
3. For each statement in the summary, decide whether it is correct. Mark any statement that is wrong, misleading or leaves out something important. If you can, say what the correct information is.
4. Make your final decision on the summary as a whole: **approve it**, **approve it with your corrections**, or **reject it**.

AI agents can make mistakes. The summary may be fully correct, or it may contain errors. Work at your normal pace; tell the researcher when you have made your final decision.

---
*Synthetic document. All names, companies, figures and dates are fictional and were created for a university study.*

paragraphs: Lark & Lantern Bakery Ltd is a craft bakery and café based in Sorrelgate, incorporated in June 2017. It is requesting a £45,000 loan over four years to replace its deck oven.
Revenue rose 7.0% to £412,000 in the year ended 31 March 2026 (previous year: £385,000). Net profit after tax increased to £31,000 from £26,000 the previous year.

The business employs 12 staff, one more than last year, and is wholly owned by Naomi Lark. Cash at bank was £18,000 at the year end (previous year: £22,000), and the business had no borrowing with the Bank at the last review.
